content.text:
All 5 tests pass, 4 remain as `it.todo`.

Over-implementation check: the survival rule is still the untouched `countLiveNeighbors === 3` — I did not add the "live cell with 2 neighbors survives" branch, since no test demands it yet (the blinker/block tests will force it). No negative-coordinate handling was added; it just falls out of the offset arithmetic. Deduplication is not speculative — the widened candidate set generates the same dead cell once per adjacent live cell, so [1,1] would otherwise appear three times in this very test.

/home/experimenter/experiments/runs/2026-07-25_23-41-36_game-of-life-example-mapping_v4-exact-subagents_opus-5/src/game-of-life.ts

```typescript
const candidates = (liveCells: Cell[]): Cell[] =>
  withoutDuplicates([...liveCells, ...liveCells.flatMap(neighborsOf)]);

export const nextGeneration = (liveCells: Cell[]): Cell[] =>
  candidates(liveCells).filter(
    (cell) => countLiveNeighbors(cell, liveCells) === 3,
  );
```

`withoutDuplicates` keys cells by `cell.toString()` (`"1,1"`) through a `Map`, keeping the first occurrence.

Green Phase Complete:
- Implementation: widened the candidate set from `liveCells` to live cells plus their eight neighbors, deduplicated by coordinate string.
- Result: all tests now pass (5 passing, 4 todo).
- Approach: minimal — the only structural blocker was that births were impossible when filtering the live set, so only the candidate set changed. The birth/survival predicate itself is unchanged.

Proceeding to Refactor phase.
